headline: A quiet weekend for prices but not for news: the FDA turned down Summit's lung cancer drug, Iran says tankers hit mines in Hormuz before oil reopens tonight, and the week still turns on Tuesday's retail sales and Nvidia report.
summary: Prices are Friday Nov 13 closes (prices_as_of 2026-11-13); markets were shut for the weekend, and Saturday's brief already corrected the 26 long term names that carried Nov 12 closes. Three things are new since Saturday. The FDA sent Summit Therapeutics a complete response letter for ivonescimab on Sunday morning because overall survival was not statistically significant (Summit, Nov 15). Iran's Revolutionary Guard said tankers hit mines in the Strait of Hormuz on Saturday; nothing was verified, and the US says it has cleared the main routes (IranWire; Gulf News). Starship's upper stage came back from orbit for the first time, while the booster skipped its catch (Space.com). The week ahead adds two new dates: Fed Chair Warsh speaks Monday at noon ET and Governor Waller Tuesday at 9:20am ET, before Nvidia reports Tuesday after the close and Anthropic prices Wednesday (Seeking Alpha; Traders and Quants). Stand aside until Tuesday night: TMO is still the only swing setup and its phone alerts have not fired.

regime.why: Nothing has traded since Friday, when QQQ closed under its 683.69 line and its 200 day and the 10 year closed at 5.15%. The weekend added Gulf risk (unverified mine claims) and no relief on rates. Oil futures reopen at 6pm ET Sunday; that is the first read.

signals.title: FDA turns down Summit's ivonescimab in EGFR mutated lung cancer: no survival win, no approval
signals.what_happened: Summit Therapeutics said at 7am ET Sunday Nov 15 that the FDA issued a complete response letter for ivonescimab with platinum chemotherapy in EGFR mutated non small cell lung cancer after EGFR TKI therapy. The FDA said the drug was not shown to work well enough without a statistically significant overall survival benefit, and that the progression free survival benefit alone does not support a positive benefit and risk balance (Summit via Business Wire). In the HARMONi trial, overall survival improved by a 21% lower risk of death but missed statistical significance (Fierce Pharma). Summit gave no resubmission plan and said it will keep running its other Phase III trials, including HARMONi-3 and HARMONi-7 (Summit). It would have been the first US approval for the PD-1 plus VEGF class (BioSpace). SMMT closed 14.15 on Nov 13, down 13.35% for that week (Massive, Saturday brief).
signals.so_what: The FDA held the line it set in advance: in this setting, overall survival is the bar, not progression free survival. That raises the bar for every PD-1 plus VEGF drug in testing, so the class now has to win on survival. Merck's Keytruda keeps its lead in lung cancer for longer. For Summit the US launch is pushed back by at least one more trial readout, and the stock has already been falling into the date. What would make this wrong: HARMONi-3, the first line trial against Keytruda, reads out with a clear survival win, which would reopen the whole class.
signals.for_you: No action. SMMT is not on a dashboard list; expect a large gap down Monday and do not buy the drop because it looks cheap. MRK (147.76, uptrend on the dashboard) is not a setup; no change to any buy zone verdict.

signals.title: Iran says tankers hit mines in Hormuz on Saturday; unverified, and oil has not traded on it yet
signals.what_happened: Iran's Revolutionary Guard said tankers struck mines and caught fire in the Strait of Hormuz on Saturday Nov 14; reports differ on two or three ships, gave no vessel names, and none were verified (IranWire; Gulf News). It warned that ships that cooperate with the US military or ignore its restrictions risk mines. The US military has said it cleared the main routes of mines and has rejected similar claims before (IranWire). Reports also cite an Iranian drone incident near Bahrain over the weekend (FinanceFeeds). Brent settled at $95.84 on Friday after a second weekly loss; futures reopen at 6pm ET Sunday (FinanceFeeds; The National).
signals.so_what: Past IRGC mine claims have not been confirmed, and oil fell for two weeks despite them, so the market may treat this as noise. If a vessel is confirmed hit, shipping insurance and freight rates rise first, then crude. A move in oil would also feed the inflation worry that has the 10 year at 5.15%, which matters more for stocks this week than the oil price itself.
signals.for_you: No action. Watch Brent at the Sunday 6pm ET open: a gap above about $98 would mean the claims are being taken seriously. No energy name is a swing setup. If you sell puts, no new ones before Tuesday anyway.

signals.title: Starship's upper stage comes back from orbit for the first time; the booster skipped its catch
signals.since_yesterday: The ship finished its 22 hour flight on Saturday and landed from orbit for the first time, per Space.com's live coverage; Musk said Sunday that slightly weak engine performance was why the booster went to a splashdown.
signals.what_happened: After launching Friday at 6:48pm ET, the Starship upper stage completed its planned flight and, per Space.com's live blog headline, 'lands from orbit for 1st time.' Scientific American also described a catch. Exact details of the tower catch were not confirmed in what could be read this morning. The Super Heavy booster had waved off its tower catch about 6.5 minutes after launch and splashed down in the Gulf of Mexico; Musk wrote Sunday that slight underperformance of the engines was the reason (Space.com).
signals.so_what: A ship that comes back whole is the step that makes the whole rocket reusable, which is the core of the cost case for Starlink V3 launches and lunar landers. The booster miss is a smaller, known problem. The money question is whether this pulls the next flight forward.
signals.for_you: No action. SPCX (139.11 on Nov 13) is not a setup. Watch Monday's volume, not the headline: only a close on heavy volume would matter.

signals.title: This week: two new Fed speeches added before retail sales, Nvidia, the 20 year sale, the minutes and Anthropic
signals.since_yesterday: Fed Chair Warsh speaks Monday at noon ET and Governor Waller Tuesday at 9:20am ET; one recap expects flat retail sales against TradingView's +0.2%; Anthropic is expected to price Wednesday and trade Thursday.
signals.what_happened: New since Saturday's week ahead. Monday Nov 16: Fed Chair Kevin Warsh gives opening remarks at a San Francisco Fed conference at noon ET (Markets Digest; Seeking Alpha); 13F filings are due; Baidu reports before the open (TradingView, unconfirmed). Tuesday Nov 17: Governor Waller speaks at 9:20am ET, after retail sales at 8:30am ET; Waller has said a core inflation print like the last one should put a half point hike on the table (Traders and Quants). Forecasts differ: TradingView shows +0.2% for retail sales (prior +0.8%), one recap expects flat with the control group +0.1%. Home Depot and Disney report before the open (unconfirmed); Nvidia reports after the close, confirmed, with Colette Kress as interim CEO while staying finance chief (Nvidia; TradingView). Wednesday Nov 18: housing starts 8:30am ET (forecast 1.268 million, prior 1.221 million); Target and Lowe's before the open (unconfirmed); 20 year bond sale at 1pm ET and Fed minutes at 2pm ET; Palo Alto Networks after the close, confirmed. In last week's 10 year sale, foreign style indirect bidders took 61.2%, down from 80.3% in October (Traders and Quants). Anthropic is expected to price its 825 million share IPO at $70 to $78 Wednesday and start trading Thursday as ANT (Seeking Alpha; RTTNews). Thursday Nov 19: Walmart and Alibaba before the open (unconfirmed); Intuit after the close, confirmed (TradingView); the Trump, Xi and Putin meeting in Shenzhen, where US officials gave mixed signals on whether chip export controls are on the table (Foreign Policy; WMAL). Friday Nov 20: monthly options expiration; Waller speaks again at 8:25am ET.
signals.so_what: Tuesday stacks a Fed speaker, retail sales and Nvidia in one day. A hot retail number plus a hawkish Waller would lift the 2 year (4.88%) and the odds of a half point hike, before Nvidia even reports. Wednesday then tests the long end twice: the 20 year sale an hour before the minutes. If indirect bidders slip again below 61.2%, long yields can rise even with no Fed news. For Nvidia, the outlook matters more than the quarter; a soft outlook would turn a leadership discount into a demand question for every AI supplier on the AI compute map.
signals.for_you: Swing: no new entries before Tuesday 4pm ET; TMO needs a close over 729.03 on 3,428,000 or more shares. Puts: expiration week; let out of the money puts expire and roll in the money ones only for a net credit and only if the name is still 'Buy zone now'; no new puts before Nvidia. Long term: no first tranche in AI group names (AMD, ENTG, ADI, SNPS) until after the report. ANT will have no chart history, so it cannot pass the dashboard's chart checks; no action.

history.when: August 2011: Steve Jobs resigns as Apple CEO
history.what: Apple fell about 5% after hours on Aug 24, 2011, then closed only 0.65% lower the next day at $373.72 (CNN Money; The Next Web).
history.lesson: A founder exit at a company with strong demand and a known successor was a one day scare. The market priced the business, not the person.

history.when: February 1994 to February 1995: the Fed's surprise tightening
history.what: The Fed doubled its target from 3% to 6% in a year and US bond losses reached about $600 billion by late 1994 (Fortune).
history.lesson: Weak auctions and rising long yields came before the stock pain; Wednesday's 20 year sale is the next auction test.

cycle.differences: Apple had a named, long planned successor and no scandal. Nvidia has an interim CEO who also stays finance chief, a board search with no timeline, and a report five days after the exit, with the stock already down 12.75% for the week. The demand question gets answered Tuesday, not the leadership question.

principle.text: Don't confuse what you wish were true with what is true (paraphrase of Principles).
principle.applied: The Summit letter is the example: a near miss on survival was hoped to be enough, and the FDA said no, as it had warned. Trade the rule that is written, not the exception you hope for.
